## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C reorganization and TRA execution

- 2012-11-13: Earlier form-of TRA filed with S-1/A for a 2012 IPO that did not consummate
- 2013-04-19: Refreshed form-of TRA filed with the 2013 S-1/A; this is the form executed at reorganization
- 2013-06-26: Corporate reorganization closes and TRA executed at 85% sharing rate with Silvercrest L.P. principals as Class B Unit holders
- 2013-07-02: IPO closes on NASDAQ under SAMG

#### Beneficiary additions via M&A (no amendment required)

- 2015-03-30: Jamison, Eaton & Wood asset acquisition; mixed cash and Class B Unit consideration, with Class B Units automatically covered by the existing TRA
- 2019-07-01: Cortina Asset Management acquisition closes; ~20% of consideration in Class B Units to Cortina principals, again folded into the existing TRA beneficiary group

## Explanation

Silvercrest Asset Management Group Inc. executed a single Tax Receivable Agreement on June 26, 2013 at its Up-C reorganization, with the IPO closing six days later on July 2, 2013. The contract pays 85% of cash tax savings to Silvercrest L.P. principals from Section 754 basis step-ups on Class B Unit exchanges, pre-IPO net operating losses and other tax assets, plus imputed interest deductions. No amendment, restatement, or termination instrument has been filed across the 2013-2026 window. Two M&A transactions (Jamison in 2015 and Cortina in 2019) added Class B Unit holders to the beneficiary group via the standard Up-C drop-down mechanism the TRA contemplated from inception, without requiring an amendment. The TRA remains in force as of the FY2024 10-K and continues to generate small periodic payments triggered by ongoing Class B-to-Class A exchanges. See `contract_log.md` for the form-of texts and the M&A drop-down treatment.
